effectiveNote: Residential purchase tax rates for a new purchase by a UK-resident individual. No transitional contracts, linked transactions, new lease rent, mixed use, company purchases, non-resident surcharges or special reliefs.
maintenanceNote: Money is in pence as integers and rates are decimals, matching rates.json. Each nation lists band upper limits, with null for the top band, and the rate charged on the part of the price inside that band. 'higherLimits' and 'higherRates' replace the standard tables when the additional-property basis applies; 'supplement' is a flat percentage of the whole price charged on top instead. Check every figure against the source links before changing them, then run npm test.
additionalMinimumNote: The additional-property charge applies only when the price is £40,000 or more, in all three nations.

england_ni.name: SDLT
england_ni.label: Stamp Duty Land Tax
england_ni.higherNote: The additional-property rates are the standard rates plus the 5% surcharge.

firstTimeBuyer.note: Nothing up to £300,000 and 5% from £300,001 to £500,000. Above £500,000 the relief is lost completely and the standard rates apply, so this table never needs an open top band.

scotland.name: LBTT and ADS
scotland.label: Land and Buildings Transaction Tax
scotland.supplementNote: 8% of the whole price for transactions on or after 5 December 2024, charged on top of LBTT.

firstTimeBuyer.note: Relief raises the nil rate band from £145,000 to £175,000; every band above is unchanged. There is no upper price limit, so the most it can save is £600, the 2% that would otherwise fall on that £30,000.

wales.name: LTT
wales.label: Land Transaction Tax
wales.higherNote: Wales has its own higher residential table rather than a surcharge, with an extra band below £180,000.
wales.firstTimeBuyerNote: Wales offers no first-time buyer relief. Its nil rate band of £225,000 is already the highest of the three, so there is no 'firstTimeBuyer' table here and first-time buyers pay the standard rates.
